notes: Inspected the indexed-record lookup and post-lookup arithmetic: x0 low byte selects a base slot, x1 is clamped, a byte at record+0xc is read, selector 0x61 is passed to an unresolved helper, then the result is adjusted and clamped to 0..100 (main_0057.c:52263-52307). The cited caller range is not the callsite: the exact indexed call is in main_0080.c:46930-46932, where arguments are prepared before invoking this function; that usage does not identify the record or returned quantity. Keep unnamed.

Confirmed body behavior: checks the enabled byte at owner+0x428; if enabled and x1 is nonnull, loads the provider at x1+8 and queries selector 0x16, converts to signed integer and adds one. A missing nested provider uses the zero-value helper then adds one; disabled returns -2, and null x1 uses x2 when nonnegative or -2 otherwise (main_0116.c:9943-9971). An indexed caller passes owner/provider and a byte-derived fallback/status value (main_0116.c:1683-1688). Name accurately captures the successful selector result without claiming domain meaning.

Confirmed: after enabled/provider checks, requests player attribute selector 0, converts the value to integer, then maps it through thresholds 15, 49, 74, 149, 299 to outputs 0, 15, 50, 75, 150, 300 (main_0112.c:34581-34633). The indexed caller passes its owner and provider and stores the returned value as a 32-bit result (main_0112.c:5017-5025). The proposed name is appropriately descriptive and avoids unsupported domain claims.

Confirmed the selector-0x16 nested provider lookup and signed-integer conversion. It returns code 2 above 20, code 1 above 10, code 3 above 4, and code 0 otherwise; disabled returns -2, while null x1 falls through to classify caller-supplied x2 (main_0119.c:9613-9650). Callers pass either -1 or a supplied status/value in x2 and consume the result as a 32-bit output (main_0117.c:9298-9305; main_0117.c:14127-14132). The name is broad enough to avoid implying a particular code ordering.

Confirmed: for nonnull x1, passes the requested integer selector in x2 to convert_attribute_value_to_float_div_100, then classifies the returned float into codes 0 through 5 using thresholds 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9 (main_0112.c:38931-38976; helper identity at 0x7001868fd4 is documented in tools/data/function_annotations.tsv). The caller passes selector 0 and stores the returned code (main_0111.c:34171-34175). Name matches the observed behavior.
